chapter: Owls, Werlein's and the OK record
title: Martin the saxophonist and Jan Garber
summary: The interviewer asks about a saxophonist named Martin, who played for Brownlee and then many years with Jan Garber.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Did you know a fellow named Martin that played saxophone?
Oh, I knew Martin that played saxophone, yes. I did.

But I had a fellow played with me by the name of Martin. I can recall now when I was playing piano he played saxophone with me. A fellow named Martin. And then right after he left me, he went with, oh, what is this fellow's name? He used to play Meyer Davis. Meyer Davis. Not Meyer Davis, but, well, it was Meyer Davis and this other name. He comes to Pensacola all the time. We went over to Mobile one time and he played over there.
Oh, let me see. Jan Garber? Jan Garber.
Garber Davis, you see, it was years ago.

But Jan Garber, this friend of mine, Martin, his home originally was Sarasota, Florida. And after he left me, he went with Jan Garber and he played with him about 11 or 12, maybe 14 years. The last I remember that I had seen him. And he was still with Garber. Very fine man.
